turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so you have twenty-five minutes, Hale. My son found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
"Over with." Owen's mark is not something you get over with, Hale. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went into the gradebook?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.
"Everyone knows it." I'm writing that down, Hale, word for word, and you can tell the principal exactly who "everyone" is. My son doesn't lie, so what do you actually have besides a machine's guess?
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.

I asked you a question, Hale, and that wasn't an answer. Your own school's procedure says you contact me before any mark is entered, and you didn't. Do you have a document with Owen's name and a date on it, or am I going upstairs?
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

Your time. My son's average is riding on this, and you've given me nothing but an insult and a software score. When I leave this room I'm going straight to the principal's office, unless that zero comes off today.
